name: niem
label: NIEM (US Government)
description: National Information Exchange Model — mandatory for US federal agency data exchange

table_notes.niem_organization: Represents any government agency, court, or law enforcement body that originates or processes NIEM data exchanges.
table_notes.niem_person: Core biographic entity for individuals in justice and public safety contexts; SSN stored as SHA-256 hash, never plaintext.
table_notes.niem_location: Physical addresses with an optional PostGIS point; referenced by incidents and other entities for geographic correlation.
table_notes.niem_incident: A reported public-safety or law-enforcement event, linked to a location and reporting agency, with NCIC-aligned category codes.
table_notes.niem_case: Legal case record tracking filing, court assignment, subject, charges, and disposition; the primary entity for court case management systems.

niem_organization.name: id
niem_organization.description: Surrogate primary key; UUID generated at insert time

niem_organization.name: name
niem_organization.description: Official full name of the agency or organization

niem_organization.name: abbreviation
niem_organization.description: Common acronym or short form (e.g. FBI, LAPD, USCG)

niem_organization.name: category
niem_organization.description: Organization type: federal, state, local, court, tribal, etc.

niem_organization.name: jurisdiction
niem_organization.description: Geographic or legal jurisdiction scope (e.g. state name, federal district)

niem_organization.name: is_active
niem_organization.description: Whether the organization is currently operational and accepting data exchanges

niem_person.name: id
niem_person.description: Surrogate primary key; UUID generated at insert time

niem_person.name: family_name
niem_person.description: Surname / last name as it appears on government identity documents

niem_person.name: given_name
niem_person.description: First / forename as it appears on government identity documents

niem_person.name: full_name
niem_person.description: Complete formatted name including middle names, prefixes, and suffixes

niem_person.name: date_of_birth
niem_person.description: Date of birth; used for identity verification and age-eligibility rules

niem_person.name: gender
niem_person.description: Gender identity; coded per NIEM nc:PersonSexCodeSimpleType vocabulary

niem_person.name: race
niem_person.description: Racial category per FBI UCR/NCIC coding standard (e.g. W, B, A, I, U)

niem_person.name: ethnicity
niem_person.description: Ethnic origin per OMB standard: Hispanic or Latino vs. Not Hispanic or Latino

niem_person.name: ssn_hash
niem_person.description: SHA-256 hex digest of SSN; enables matching without storing plaintext PII

niem_person.name: state_id
niem_person.description: State-issued driver’s license or ID number for secondary identity matching

niem_location.name: id
niem_location.description: Surrogate primary key; UUID generated at insert time

niem_location.name: address_line
niem_location.description: Street number, street name, unit/suite; free-form per USPS addressing rules

niem_location.name: state_code
niem_location.description: USPS two-letter state/territory abbreviation (e.g. CA, TX, PR)

niem_location.name: zip
niem_location.description: USPS ZIP or ZIP+4 code for postal routing and geographic approximation

niem_location.name: country
niem_location.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (default US for domestic records)

niem_location.name: geo_point
niem_location.description: PostGIS WGS84 point; enables ST_DWithin proximity and ST_Distance queries

niem_incident.name: id
niem_incident.description: Surrogate primary key; UUID generated at insert time

niem_incident.name: incident_number
niem_incident.description: Agency-assigned incident report number; unique within the reporting agency

niem_incident.name: incident_type
niem_incident.description: Narrative incident classification (e.g. Burglary, Traffic Stop, Domestic Disturbance)

niem_incident.name: category_code
niem_incident.description: NIBRS/UCR offense category code aligning with FBI National Incident-Based Reporting System

niem_incident.name: location_id
niem_incident.description: References niem_location.id; pinpoints where the incident occurred

niem_incident.name: reported_at
niem_incident.description: Timestamp when the incident was officially reported to the agency (timezone-aware)

niem_incident.name: occurred_at
niem_incident.description: Estimated or known timestamp when the incident actually took place

niem_incident.name: status
niem_incident.description: Current lifecycle status: open, cleared, unfounded, inactive, closed

niem_incident.name: narrative
niem_incident.description: Free-text officer narrative describing the incident in detail

niem_incident.name: reporting_org_id
niem_incident.description: References niem_organization.id; identifies the agency that filed this incident report

niem_case.name: id
niem_case.description: Surrogate primary key; UUID generated at insert time

niem_case.name: case_number
niem_case.description: Court-assigned docket or case number; unique within the court’s jurisdiction

niem_case.name: case_type
niem_case.description: Case category: criminal, civil, juvenile, traffic, domestic, etc.

niem_case.name: status
niem_case.description: Procedural status: pending, active, disposed, appealed, closed

niem_case.name: filing_date
niem_case.description: Date the case was formally filed with the court

niem_case.name: court_id
niem_case.description: References niem_organization.id; identifies the court where the case is docketed

niem_case.name: subject_id
niem_case.description: References niem_person.id; the defendant or primary subject of the case

niem_case.name: charges
niem_case.description: Array of charge objects: [{statute, description, degree, count, amended_from}]

niem_case.name: disposition
niem_case.description: Final outcome: guilty, not guilty, dismissed, pled, deferred adjudication, etc.

short_description: National Information Exchange Model — mandatory for US federal agency data exchange
long_description: NIEM (National Information Exchange Model) is the US federal government's framework for sharing information across agencies and jurisdictions. The schema implements core NIEM justice and public safety entities: organizations (agencies), persons with biographic and identifier data, geographic locations, incidents (reported events), and legal cases with charge/disposition tracking.
when_to_use: Use for law enforcement records management systems, court case management, emergency dispatch (CAD) systems, or any federal contractor building inter-agency data sharing solutions. NIEM compliance is required for NCIC (National Crime Information Center) integration, DOJ grants, and DHS/FEMA contracts. State courts increasingly mandate NIEM-aligned data exchange for criminal justice systems.
